headline: Travel Money & Payments · Spanish · Foundation
threshold: Use Spanish to complete the foundation travel money & payments conversations and explain the next step.

lessons.title: Ask how much something costs
lessons.objective: Ask the price of one item and of two items, identify the currency, and repeat each amount back to the seller.
lessons.focus: Price questions with cuesta and cuestan: the verb agrees with one item or with several items.

words.note: Masculine: el melón, los melones. The written accent marks stress on the last syllable.
A small yellow or green citrus fruit; in Spanish it is masculine, so use el limón.
The amount asked for an item. In many places cuánto vale is also heard in shops.
The currency name stays the same in singular and plural: un euro, dos euros.
A place with stalls where people buy food and goods.
A woman who sells goods. The masculine form is vendedor.
The full amount after every item is added together.
A bag for carrying purchases. In shops it may cost extra.
A general word for fresh fruit sold at a stall.

words.en: How much does this melon cost?
words.note: A complete question for asking one price. Point to the item while you ask.

words.en: How much do two lemons cost?
words.note: Use cuestan because more than one item is being priced.

words.en: How much is it in total?
words.note: Asks for the sum of everything you have chosen.

words.en: I will take it, thank you.
words.note: Said when you decide to buy. Lo refers to the item already named.

words.en: Can you give me a bag?
words.note: Polite request; puede is the usted form of poder.

lessons.speaking: You are buying fruit at a market stall. Ask the price of one melon and of two lemons, then repeat each amount back in euros. Close by saying the melon is the one you will take, and thank the vendor.
lessons.partnerRole: Fruit vendor at a Spanish-speaking weekly market
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué le pongo hoy? Tenemos melones muy dulces.

lessons.title: Read prices and decimal amounts
lessons.objective: Read a price with a decimal comma and say whole euros and cents in Spanish, then confirm the total.
lessons.focus: Decimal comma in prices, cents after the comma, and the agreement of un euro and dos euros.

words.note: The smaller unit of the euro; one euro has one hundred cents.
In prices written in Spanish, the comma separates euros from cents.
The person who makes or sells bread in a bakery.
A shop that sells bread and other baked goods.
Often sold in bottles at small shops and kiosks.
The sum of all prices before you pay.
A person who buys goods or services.
A basic baked food sold by weight or by the loaf.
The currency unit; the plural is euros.

words.es: El pan cuesta dos euros con cincuenta céntimos.
words.en: The bread costs two euros and fifty cents.
words.note: Say the full amount in words when you want to be sure of the price.
Repeat the amount back to check it. Use the decimal comma shown on the price.

words.es: Los céntimos van después de la coma.
words.en: The cents come after the comma.
words.note: A clear way to explain how to read a price with cents.

words.es: Le devuelvo un euro con treinta céntimos.
words.en: I will give you back one euro and thirty cents.
words.note: Said by the seller when returning change.

words.es: Pago con un billete de cinco euros.
words.en: I will pay with a five-euro note.
words.note: Tells the seller which banknote you will use.

lessons.speaking: You are buying bread and bottled water at a bakery counter. Say the price of each item in full, using euros and cents, then add them together and confirm the total with the baker.
lessons.partnerRole: Baker at a neighborhood bakery who checks each price aloud
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué le sirvo? El pan de hoy está recién horneado.

lessons.title: Recognize banknotes and coins
lessons.objective: Identify banknotes and coins by value, ask what a note is worth, and choose the coins needed for a small fare.
lessons.focus: Indefinite articles un, una, unos and unas, and de with the value of a note or coin.

words.note: A metal piece of money. Moneda also means currency in general.
A paper note of money, such as a five-euro note.
A small stand that sells newspapers, drinks and tickets.
A woman who works in a shop or kiosk. The masculine form is dependiente.
A large public vehicle that stops along a route.
The currency name used for coins and notes.
The number or sum of money you need or pay.
Used when a payment matches the price without change. It agrees with the noun it describes.
The coins or notes given back when you pay more than the price.

words.en: How much is this coin worth?
words.note: A natural way to ask a coin's value, common in shops and kiosks.
Asks for coins of a particular value.

words.en: That is exactly three euros, right?
words.note: Confirms the amount and invites the seller to agree.

words.en: Do you have change for five euros?
words.note: Useful when you need smaller notes or coins.
A common closing phrase in small shops.

lessons.speaking: You are at a newsstand with a five-euro note and only small coins. Ask what one coin is worth, then ask for the right number of one-euro coins for a bus fare of three euros, and confirm the total before you pay.
lessons.partnerRole: Newsstand attendant who explains coins and notes calmly
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué necesita? Si quiere, le ayudo con el cambio.

lessons.title: Ask whether cash or card is accepted
lessons.objective: Confirm whether a shop accepts cash or card before buying, and state your own payment method clearly.
lessons.focus: Yes/no questions with aceptar, and pagar con or pagar en to name the payment method.

words.note: Money in notes and coins. Pagar en efectivo means paying with cash.
A plastic payment card. Tarjeta de crédito and tarjeta de débito are different cards.
The amount owed in a restaurant or café.
A man who serves food and drinks in a restaurant. The feminine form is camarera.
The act or amount of paying for something.
A written proof that you have paid.
The machine on the counter that processes card payments.
A sweet baked dessert, often sold by the slice.
A hot drink made from coffee beans, and also the place that serves it.
A complete question to ask before ordering or paying.
Use puedo with an infinitive for a permission question.

words.en: I will pay in cash, please.
words.note: Tells the staff your choice before the bill is added.

words.es: Le traigo el recibo ahora mismo.
words.en: I will bring you the receipt right now.
words.note: Said by the waiter when the payment is finished.
A polite way to hand over payment.

lessons.speaking: You enter a café and want a coffee and a cake. Ask if the café accepts credit cards, ask whether cash is also accepted, then choose the method you will use and confirm the amount with the waiter.
lessons.partnerRole: Waiter at a busy café who accepts both cash and cards
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Qué desea tomar? Tenemos café, té y pasteles.

lessons.title: Pay with a larger banknote
lessons.objective: Hand over a larger banknote, ask the seller to change it, and use object pronouns such as me lo and se lo when speaking about the note.
lessons.focus: Object pronouns before a conjugated verb or attached to an infinitive, and se lo when le and lo appear together.

words.note: A paper note of money. Use the plural billetes when you mean several notes.
The money returned when a payment is larger than the price.
A man who works in a shop. The feminine form is dependienta.
A drink made from fruit. In some regions jugo is used instead.
A place where goods are sold, usually smaller than a supermarket.
Used in greetings after dark, for example buenas noches.
The smaller unit of euro money. Cents follow euros with con or y.
A general word for an item or amount you have not named.
The plural of moneda. Coins are often given as change, so ask for them by value.

words.en: Can you change it for me?
words.note: Asks for change of a larger note in a polite form.

words.es: Le doy este billete de veinte euros.
words.en: I will give you this twenty-euro note.
words.note: Used to hand over payment and name its value at the same time.

words.en: I do not have change for twenty.
words.note: A shop worker's common reply when a large note is offered.

words.en: I will change it for you right now.
words.note: Le becomes se before lo: se lo cambio, never le lo cambio.

words.es: Su cambio son siete euros con cincuenta céntimos.
words.en: Your change is seven euros and fifty cents.
words.note: Said when the seller returns change after paying.

lessons.speaking: You want a small bottle of juice but only have a twenty-euro note. Tell the seller you will pay with it, ask whether they can change it, and accept the change when it is given back. Close by thanking them and confirming the amount.
lessons.partnerRole: Shop assistant at a corner grocery who has few small notes
lessons.openingLine: Buenas noches. ¿Desea algo más? Tenemos zumo de naranja fresco.

lessons.title: Count and confirm your change
lessons.objective: Subtract a simple price from a cash payment, say the change aloud in Spanish, and check it with the cashier before leaving.
lessons.focus: Numbers with cents read as units of euros and céntimos, and the verb contar used to count money aloud.

words.note: The money returned after a payment that is larger than the price. Usually said with the cashier counting it back.
A woman who takes payments at a till. The masculine form is cajero.
A filled bread snack. Pronounced with the stress on the first syllable.
A paper note of money. Say billete de diez euros for a ten-euro note.
The full amount you must pay after items are added.
The small unit of the euro; in amounts the cents follow the euros.
The arithmetic of taking the price away from the amount paid. Often used when checking change.
A paper or digital record that a payment was made.
A hot drink, and also the place that serves coffee.

words.es: Son seis euros con cuarenta céntimos.
words.en: It is six euros and forty cents.
words.note: Said by the cashier when giving the total with cents.

words.es: Le doy un billete de diez euros.
words.en: I will give you a ten-euro note.
words.note: Tells the cashier the note you will use for payment.

words.es: Cuento en voz alta el cambio.
words.en: I count the change out loud.
words.note: Lets the cashier hear your check before you leave.
The usual phrase when a cashier gives money back.

words.es: ¿Me puede dar el recibo, por favor?
words.en: Can you give me the receipt, please?
words.note: A complete polite request for proof of payment.

lessons.speaking: You buy a sandwich and a coffee that together cost six euros and forty cents, and you pay with a ten-euro note. Work out the change in your head, say it aloud, and ask the cashier to confirm it. Close by saying the change is correct and that you do not need a receipt.
lessons.partnerRole: Cashier at a small bakery who counts change back to the customer
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Qué le sirvo? Tenemos sándwiches frescos y café recién hecho.

lessons.title: Ask for a receipt
lessons.objective: Ask for a receipt and check the amount, date and currency printed on it before you leave the counter.
lessons.focus: Question words qué and cuál for asking what is on a document, and the agreement of el importe and la fecha.

words.note: A written record of a payment. Ask for it when you need proof.
The sum of money shown on a document or ticket.
The day, month and year printed on a receipt.
The type of money used in a payment; not the same as a coin.
A woman who works for a business. The masculine form is empleado.
A document showing that a payment was made. Common in Latin America.
A journey there and back; British English says return ticket. Ask for un billete de ida y vuelta.
Used when two amounts or details agree with each other.
A trip from one place to another.

words.en: Can you give me a receipt, please?
words.note: A polite request for proof of payment at a counter.

words.en: What details do you need to appear?
words.note: A clerk's question about what the receipt will show.
Reads the key details of a receipt in order.

words.es: Todo coincide con lo que pagué.
words.note: Confirms the check you have made against the receipt.

words.es: Guarde el comprobante para cualquier cambio.
words.en: Keep the proof of payment in case you change the trip.
words.note: Advice given when a document may be needed later.

lessons.speaking: You are at a rail ticket office where you paid for a return journey. Ask for a receipt, tell the clerk which details you need, and read back the amount, date and currency to check them. Close by thanking the clerk and confirming the receipt is right.
lessons.partnerRole: Ticket clerk at a rail office who prints receipts
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Para qué viaje necesita el recibo?

lessons.title: Ask what is included in a price
lessons.objective: Ask whether a ticket price includes an extra item, service or charge and understand the answer before you pay.
lessons.focus: The verb incluir and the question form ¿Incluye…?, plus the adverb aparte for something separate.

words.note: The ticket that lets you into a place, such as a museum or a show.
A woman who sells tickets at a counter. The masculine form is taquillero.
A device or app that explains a place while you walk around.
The amount asked for an item or entry.
A charge set by a government and added to some prices. Its name and rate depend on the country.
A charge or work done for a customer, shown separately in some bills.
An amount added to a price or bill. Use the plural cargos for several charges.
Describes an item already counted in the price.
A trip to see a place, such as a museum.

words.en: Does the price include the audio guide?
words.note: Ask this before paying to avoid an unexpected extra cost.

words.es: La audioguía cuesta tres euros aparte.
words.en: The audio guide costs three euros separately.
words.note: Said by the seller to show an item charged on its own.

words.en: Does the entry include all the charges?
words.note: Checks whether the total is the final amount.

words.en: I will decide about the audio guide later.
words.note: A clear way to delay a purchase while still paying for the entry.
A common polite closing phrase from staff.

lessons.speaking: You are buying a museum ticket and want to know whether the audio guide is included. Ask about the audio guide and about other charges, understand the answer, and decide whether to buy the guide separately. Close by paying for the entry and thanking the clerk.
lessons.partnerRole: Ticket desk clerk at a small city museum
lessons.openingLine: Buenos días. ¿Quiere una entrada normal o reducida?

lessons.title: Ask about a discount
lessons.objective: Ask politely whether a discount is available, understand a clerk's conditional answer and decide whether to accept it.
lessons.focus: Yes/no questions with ¿Tiene algún descuento…? and the use of algún before a masculine noun, plus si for a conditional offer.

words.note: A reduction in the usual price. Ask for it with tener un descuento.
A person who studies at a school or university.
A printed or electronic book sold in a bookshop.
A shop that sells books.
A lower price on an item, often shown on a sign.
A special price or promotion for a limited time.
Used with a number to say a share of the price, such as 10 por ciento.
A new item in a shop, often a new book or record.
The full amount after any discount is added or taken away.

words.en: Do you have any student discount?
words.note: A polite question to ask before the clerk sets the price.

words.en: If I buy two books, is there a discount?
words.note: Asks about a conditional offer before you choose.

words.es: Me parece bien. Llevo los dos.
words.en: That sounds good to me. I will take both.
words.note: Accepts an offer and confirms the purchase.

words.en: No, thank you. I prefer to buy one.
words.note: Declines the offer politely with a clear reason.

words.es: El total con descuento es 23,40 euros.
words.en: The total with the discount is 23.40 euros.
words.note: Confirms the final amount in euros and cents.

lessons.speaking: You are at a bookshop with a student card and want to buy two books. Ask whether there is a student discount, ask what happens if you buy two books, and accept or decline the offer. Close by confirming the total you will pay.
lessons.partnerRole: Bookshop assistant who explains a store offer
lessons.openingLine: Buenas tardes. ¿Busca algún libro en particular? Tenemos novedades este mes.

lessons.title: Complete a small cash purchase
lessons.objective: Complete a small cash purchase from start to finish: confirm the price, explain that the card reader is unavailable, check the change and close the exchange.
lessons.focus: No funciona for a machine that is out of order, solo meaning only, and the usted command espere.

words.note: The surface where a worker takes orders or payments.
The machine that takes card payments.
Money in notes and coins, not card.
A small sponge cake, often sold with coffee in Spain.
A hot drink. Ask for café con leche for coffee with milk.
Money returned after a larger payment.
A paper note of money.
The small unit of the euro.
The full amount added together.

words.es: ¿Cuánto son un café y una magdalena?
words.en: How much are a coffee and a muffin?
words.note: Asks the total for two items with the plural form son.
Asks which payment method is accepted before you hand over money.

words.es: Lo siento, la terminal no funciona hoy.
words.en: I am sorry, the card reader is not working today.
words.note: Explains why a card payment cannot be made.

words.es: Entonces pago con un billete de cinco euros.
words.en: Then I will pay with a five-euro note.
words.note: Chooses the cash method and states the note.

words.es: Cuento el cambio: cincuenta céntimos, correcto.
words.en: I count the change: fifty cents, correct.
words.note: Confirms the change aloud before leaving.

lessons.speaking: You want a coffee and a muffin at a station kiosk, but the card reader is not working. Confirm the total, pay with a five-euro note, count the change, and close the exchange. Say that you will wait a moment if they need to check the machine.
lessons.partnerRole: Kiosk attendant at a busy railway station whose card reader is not working today
lessons.openingLine: Buenas. ¿Qué le pongo? Hoy tenemos magdalenas recién hechas.
